projects.title: Guangzhou PV Sunroom Project
projects.summary: A 25.8 kW PV sunroom combining shade, weather protection and clean power generation.
projects.requirements: Replace a conventional glass sunroom with a PV roof that provides insulation, waterproofing and electricity generation.
projects.background: The owner wanted a more comfortable terrace and better use of the roof while addressing summer heat and rainwater leakage.
projects.solution: The system uses a Solis G5-GR3P(12-25)K(21A) three-phase PV inverter. Its 21 A string input and up to 1000 V input accommodate high-efficiency and bifacial modules. IP66 protection supports outdoor installation.
projects.results: PV modules provide shade and reduce direct solar heat|The integrated roof reduces leakage risk|The 25.8 kW installation supplies clean electricity, with surplus available for grid export|The roof and terrace gain practical year-round value

projects.title: Zengcheng Villa PV Sunroom Project
projects.summary: A 30.2 kW villa PV sunroom designed to make the terrace useful throughout the year.
projects.requirements: Keep the terrace open and bright while reducing summer heat and rainy-season leakage, with on-site power generation.
projects.background: The owner wanted to improve comfort and the value of the terrace without losing its open view.
projects.solution: PV modules form the sunroom roof in place of conventional glass. A 30.2 kW system is matched with a Solis G6-GR3P(30-40)K three-phase inverter. Generated power is used by the villa first, with surplus fed into the grid.
projects.results: The PV roof blocks direct sunlight and improves comfort|Fewer roof seams reduce leakage risk|The 30.2 kW system provides clean electricity|The terrace becomes a more useful leisure space in every season

projects.title: Vietnam Commercial Rooftop PV Project
projects.summary: A 31.68 kW commercial rooftop PV system using factory roof space to reduce grid electricity use.
projects.requirements: Use the existing factory roof for solar generation, reducing grid dependence and long-term electricity costs.
projects.background: The owner sought more predictable energy costs through on-site generation. Updated Vietnamese rooftop solar rules may also create options for eligible surplus electricity.
projects.solution: The 31.68 kW system is tailored to the roof area and load profile. It uses a Solis S5-GC(25-50)K three-phase inverter with 3/4 MPPTs for mixed roof orientations. IP66 protection and fanless cooling suit hot, humid conditions. Power is used on site first; surplus is handled under applicable rules.
projects.results: Self-consumption reduces electricity drawn from the grid|Existing roof space becomes a clean-energy asset|The inverter is designed for hot, humid and variable-grid conditions|The system supports future surplus-power use and greener production

projects.title: Chile Commercial & Industrial PV Project
projects.summary: A 63 kW commercial PV installation designed for a future battery-storage upgrade.
projects.requirements: Reduce grid electricity use with solar generation while retaining the option to add storage later.
projects.background: The owner wanted to manage high commercial electricity costs and keep the system ready for a later PV-plus-storage expansion.
projects.solution: The project uses a 63 kW PV array with a Solis S6-EH3P50K-H three-phase hybrid inverter. It supports four MPPTs, PV input up to 1000 V and a 150–800 V battery-voltage range, allowing compatible battery storage to be added later.
projects.results: Solar power is used on site first to reduce grid draw|The hybrid inverter keeps a storage upgrade available|The equipment is designed to tolerate local grid fluctuations
